conductivity and formation permeability on the well inflow performance (see Cinco-
Ley, SPE 10043, 1982 for a review).  A widely used correlation is that published by
Cinco-Ley and Samaniego (JPT, 1981, 1749-1766) in which {r'w/Lf}, or effective
wellbore radius divided by conductive fracture length, is plotted against the
dimensionless fracture conductivity (FCD). This is illustrated in Figure 5.  This Figure
shows that a FCD value of 15 is required to ensure that the well inflow is not being
limited by the fracture conductivity.  An alternative presentation (Figure 6) allows the
(negative) skin effect due to the propped hydraulic fracture (Sf) to be calculated from
